w: Fossils of 24 Columbian mammoths lie here, killed not all at once but across three episodes -- likely repeated flash floods trapping herds on the same ground. It is the largest known concentration of mammoths killed by a single recurring event, excavated in place and preserved as a National Monument since 2015.
s: Mass mammoth graveyard, killed by flash floods
_facts: Fossils of 24 Columbian mammoths plus other Pleistocene animals
Largest known site of mammoths dying from a recurring event, likely flash floods
Deaths occurred across three separate episodes, not simultaneously
Designated a National Monument in 2015 via a city/Baylor/NPS partnership

w: Opened in November 1869, this single-span suspension bridge over the Brazos was the longest of its kind west of the Mississippi -- built by the firm that later raised the Brooklyn Bridge. It replaced a slow, dangerous ferry crossing on the Chisholm Trail, and still draws crowds every Fourth of July for fireworks.
s: 1869 bridge, once the longest span west of the Mississippi
_facts: Built by the firm that later built the Brooklyn Bridge
Key crossing on the Chisholm Trail cattle route
Contains nearly 3 million bricks; site of an annual July 4 fireworks gathering
